angle: new_interface_method on a generic base interface (CloseIterator[T]) that propagates through a two-level type-alias chain to all EntryIterator and SampleIterator concrete implementations across the entire loki pkg/ tree
difficulty_notes: The cascade is indirect and requires understanding Go generics embedding: CloseIterator[T] is embedded into StreamIterator[T] which is aliased to EntryIterator and SampleIterator. Models that search for 'CloseIterator' implementors directly will find zero results (no struct directly says 'implements CloseIterator') — they must reason through the alias chain. The breadth is the other challenge: implementations are scattered across 7+ source files in 5 different packages (iter/, chunkenc/, storage/, querier/, logql/). Models will typically find the obvious ones in pkg/iter/ but miss the deep-package ones in chunkenc/, storage/batch.go, and logql/evaluator.go. Additionally, the noOpIterator[T] and errorIterator[T] generics in iterator.go are easily overlooked — they look like trivial stubs but they DO implement the full interface and must gain Context().
